name: Keystones
slug: Magical stones used to open and connect Atlas’s Arch realms
description: The Keystones are a set of eight magical stones corresponding to the Arch realms of Atlas, created by the Navi by distilling knowledge from the rings of the Eldarin Tree. They are used with the arches to open or connect the realms and are entrusted to keepers who are expected to use and protect them. Their creation unintentionally initiated the Mother’s Prayer. Six keystones are currently assigned to party members: Gerk holds Midgard, Sylan holds Gilbrick, Dana holds Pitel, Walker holds The Reach, Ord holds Feldspar, and Ciri holds Lith. The La-rel and Turof keystones remain unassigned and are in Juten Prime’s care.

log.summary: The party intends to retain guardianship of the keystones they have claimed, while leaving the La-rel and Turof keystones in Juten Prime's care. The ruined archives may have contained information explaining how to use the keystones, potentially providing a clue to Grixto's knowledge.

log.summary: Session planning notes that the party's six assigned keystones grant access to six of Atlas's eight Arch realms, giving them enough control over arch connections to manipulate inter-realm trade if they choose—an option raised in connection with potential economic pressure against the lich.
notes: The party currently has access to six of Atlas's eight Arch realms, enough to manipulate inter-realm trade if they choose.

log.summary: The delivery to Juten Prime is finished, and the keystones are back in the party's care because the prophecy elevated their role; Carlkin had not been told. Sylan confirms four are in the lighthouse. Carlkin speaks of thirty keystones that connect the worlds. Dana says the party are all gatekeepers and that they hold the keystones, and Carlkin accepts that. A key seated in a built gate opens only to a predetermined place, narrower than what a gatekeeper can do. Once all of them are placed in one gatehouse, the gatekeepers are more or less obligated to remain there, dormant, and protect that hub. A Doorman changed by a keystone will likely be asked to open portals tied to that stone. Using one away from a gatehouse would require a powerful ley-line crossing; the party has tried and, except for Gerk's doors, has not succeeded. Grixto wants the keystones, which is why the party is hunting him. Carlkin warns that a keystone could have been lost with Gerk if the nowhere-door had taken him, and he does not know the result.
